subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the parabola whose vertex is (3, −2), focus is (3, 1).

mark_split.label: Find the direction of the axis and the value of a

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Maths-2B, book p.83 — VSAQ chapter 14 Parabola, answer 126.1, the first of a printed twin pair on a two-column page. Printed appearances: TS 2018, 2019, 2022; AP 2017. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, same page-format reasoning as the rest of this chapter. No two-book union check was possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material is on hand), and no board back-test beyond diffing against this book's own five Guess Papers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the axis direction and a
steps.margin_note: First mark, for the direction of the axis and a = 3.
lines: Given vertex A = (3, −2), focus S = (3, 1). The x-coordinates of A and S are equal, so the axis is parallel to the y-axis.
Since S lies above A, the parabola opens vertically upward.
steps.why: Two points with the same x-coordinate lie on a vertical line, so the axis must be parallel to the y-axis; which way the parabola opens follows from which of the two points, vertex or focus, is higher up.
common_mistakes: Comparing the y-coordinates instead of the x-coordinates to decide the axis direction.
Writing a = 9 instead of a = 3 by forgetting to take the square root.
steps.memory_tip: Equal x-coordinates mean a vertical axis; the focus sitting above the vertex means the parabola opens upward.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for the correct equation with the sign of 4a matching the upward direction.
lines: An upward parabola with vertex (h,k) is (x−h)² = 4a(y−k).
steps.why: Once the direction and a are known, the vertex form (x−h)² = 4a(y−k) is a direct substitution — no further derivation needed.
common_mistakes: Using (x−h)² = −4a(y−k), the downward form, by mixing up the two cases.
Writing y−(−2) as y−2 instead of y+2.
steps.memory_tip: Upward parabola: (x−h)² = 4a(y−k). Downward: the same with a minus sign in front of 4a.

insider_note: Deciding upward or downward before writing the equation is the step that actually earns the mark — the substitution afterward is routine.
